add_plan.description: Use this for a rate or plan change. Usage from this date is priced with the new plan. Earlier usage keeps the plan it was recorded under.

menu_options.add_plan: Add a plan from a date (rate or plan change)
menu_options.demand: Demand charge (a monthly fee based on your peak kW)

demand.title: Demand charge: which plan?
demand.description: Choose the plan this demand charge belongs to.

devices.title: Tracked devices
devices.description: Pick other energy sensors (kWh) to price with this contract, for example an EV charger. Each one gets cost today, month to date and lifetime sensors. Deselecting a device removes its sensors.

demand_values.title: Demand charge
demand_values.description:
Some plans charge a daily fee for every kW of your highest demand that month. On your bill this is the line **Demand (kW/Day)**: the number before 'KW' is the billed kW for that month, and the rate is the dollar amount after it.

Enter the rate, then one line for each month you were billed, for example:
`2025-01: 13.2`
`2025-02: 10.1`

Leave the months empty if your plan has no demand charge.

**Estimate from my meter:** switch this on to have Power Bill work out your highest demand itself from your import meter, so the month's demand charge shows up before the bill arrives. A kW you enter for a month always replaces the estimate. Set the hours and block length to match your bill (for example 'Demand 7 days a week: 4:00pm to 9:00pm').

data.demand_rate: Demand rate (AUD per kW per day)

data_description.demand_rate: The rate on the Demand line of your bill, for example 0.185.
data_description.demand_kw: One month per line as YYYY-MM: kW. Use the kW printed on that month's bill.
data_description.demand_estimate: Needs about a week of 5-minute meter history. Months you enter above are never overridden.
data_description.demand_block_minutes: Most retailers use 30. The highest average over one block, starting on the clock, is your demand.

feed_in.title: Stepped feed-in: which plan?
feed_in.description: Choose the plan this feed-in rule belongs to.

feed_in_values.title: Stepped feed-in
feed_in_values.description:
Some solar feed-in tariffs pay a higher rate for the first few kWh you export each day, and a lower rate after that. On your bill these appear as **Solar FiT - Step 1** and **Step 2**.

Set the daily limit to 0 to switch this off. Only plans with a single feed-in band can use this.

data.daily_cap: Step 1 covers this many kWh per day

data_description.step_1_rate: The higher rate, paid on the first kWh each day.
data_description.daily_cap: For example 8 means the first 8 kWh exported each day are paid at step 1.
data_description.step_2_rate: The lower rate, paid on everything above the daily limit.

provider.title: Energy provider name
provider.description: The name on your bill, for example 1st Energy. Changing it renames the device and its sensors. Entity IDs don't change.
